A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have demonstrated the first successful operation of a high-order vector vortex coronagraph at L' band on the NACO instrument on the Very Large Telescope.
the AGPM coronagraph is a very powerful instrument, that can be installed on any adaptive optics system, and can be operated by any user, to perform high contrast observations at L'.
we have developed a novel coronagraphic concept for the L-band, the L'-band AGPM, that has been successfully tested on-sky.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the L'-band AGPM coronagraph has a high throughput (about 80% of the diffraction pattern), and is able to suppress the diffraction spikes from the central star, as well as the speckles that are generated by the telescope.

the AGPM vector vortex is the first coronagraphic concept that is able to deliver high-contrast images in a wide range of wavelengths and for a wide range of targets (from hot stars to cold brown dwarfs) without the need for any other instrument than a high-resolution imaging spectrograph.
the AGPM coronagraph can be operated in a stable way for long exposures, with a throughput of 40-50%, and a contrast level of 10-6 in the inner 2 arcsec.
